page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.6xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 24 dedicated x86_64 physical cores using AMD EPYC 9R05 processors operating at clock speeds up to 5.0 GHz, configured with one thread per core. The compute hardware supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and bfloat16, alongside 96 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 system memory (4 GB per core). This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage while providing 50 Gbps of baseline network throughput.

Benchmark evaluations indicate upper-echelon processing capability across both single-threaded and multi-threaded tasks. With a Geekbench single-core score of 3,108 and multi-core score of 28,537, the instance demonstrates exceptional instruction throughput driven by its 5.0 GHz clock rate and dedicated core mapping. Memory bandwidth is similarly prominent, achieving 402.87 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 198.46 GB/sec in write operations. Furthermore, the EPYC processor achieves top-tier results in integer compression tasks, database operational tests, and CPU-based LLM token generation across small and medium parameter profiles.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation eliminates hyper-threading contention, translating into reliable, deterministic CPU latency. However, the complete omission of onboard NVMe storage necessitates external EBS volumes, requiring architectural consideration of storage I/O constraints. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of high-frequency compute and high-speed DDR5 memory, offering favorable processing yields for workloads that demand steady single-core execution alongside high sustained multi-core performance.

The m8azn.6xlarge instance is ideally configured for compute-intensive enterprise applications, relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration and build pipelines, high-concurrency static web serving, and CPU-driven vector and machine learning inference tasks that benefit from AVX-512 extensions and wide memory bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.6xlarge is a high-performance general-purpose instance featuring 24 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R05 physical cores at up to 5.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Backed by the Nitro system, the platform pairs its high-frequency x86_64 processor with 96 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory and 50 Gbps baseline networking. It includes support for vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and bfloat16, but provides no integrated GPU hardware or local storage. In benchmark assessments, the m8azn.6xlarge demonstrates top-tier single-core and multi-core performance, coupled with memory read bandwidth exceeding 400 GB/sec and exceptional database processing metrics. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without virtualization thread contention. This configuration delivers robust throughput for relational database operations, demanding continuous integration pipelines, high-throughput web architectures, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
